chapter: Gambling, Cab's small groups and Havana
title: Lucky Millinder's perfect four at a crap game and his spiritualist side
summary: At a Charleston station Lucky made a hard four first roll on someone else's dice; Francis says he was psychic and worked as Professor Wilson, a spiritualist, in the South.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Well, I tell you -- one of the things that used to happen in that band was we used to have a lot of crap games going on, and one night we finished playing in Charleston, South Carolina at the North Station -- I think that's the station in Charleston, waiting for the train to come in.

So we got a crap game going on outside the station there, when up walks Lucky, and Lucky pulls out $50, and he bet anyone that he could make four on the dice, for $50. Well, as anyone who shoots dice knows, 10 and 4 are the two hardest points to make.
He lost a fortune trying to do it?
Do you know that he picked up those

dice, and rolled them out there the first time, and made four, two deuces? And everybody stood up there with their mouths open, because they don't know to this day, how he did it, whether he had done it straight or whether he had cheated or what. But it was not his dice; the dice belonged to one of the other guys in the band.
And Lucky took those dice and made a perfect four the first time out -- that's why his name was Lucky; he was the luckiest man in the world.
I hear he was a very psychic man and a very exciting man; that he used to do things like that quite often.
Was it later on in his life that he went on to some sort of spiritual thing?
Do you know anything about that?

Well, no, I don't know too much about that; all I know is that he used to go down south where he was known as Professor Wilson, the spiritualist, and he used to come back to New York with bags of money that he made, you know, down south.
But he was a very psychic man. Very psychic, you know? He was able to say that such and such a thing was going to happen, and it would happen exactly as he said it would.
